senses: to fade away, or die out
la:verb:evanesco.html:
ē-vānesco, nŭi, 3 (
part. fut. evaniturus, ), v. inch. n., to vanish or pass away, to die away, to disappear (class.).
Lit.
In gen.: Bacchi cum flos evanuit (with diffugere in auras),: evanescere paulatim et decrescere pondus,: evanescere stinguique colorem,: pruna,: aquae,to evaporate,; cf.: vinum et salsamentum vetustate,i. e. to lose its strength, become vapid,: cornuaque extremae velut evanescere lunae, et saep.: et procul in tenuem ex oculis evanuit auram,; ; .—
Of persons who flee or hide themselves through fear, ; . —
Trop.: ne cum poëta scriptura evanesceret, to die away, sink into oblivion, prol. alt. 5; cf.: omnis eorum memoria sensim obscurata est et evanuit,: orationes,: Hortensius,: sententiae Aristonis, Pyrrhonis (opp. stabilitatem habere), et saep.: postea quam extenuari spem nostram et evanescere vidi,: rumor,; : fama,: ingenium,: omnis vis herbarum,: bella per taedia et moras (opp. valida impetu),: donatio, i. e. to lose its effect (opp. valere), ; cf.: actio dotis,: evanescunt haec atque emoriuntur comparatione meliorum,.

la:verb:evolo.gloss: to fly away, up or out
senses: to fly away, up or out
la:verb:evolo.html:
ē-vŏlo, āvi, ātum, 1, v. n.,
to fly out or forth, to fly away, to fly up (class.).
Lit.: ex quercu (aquila),: extra septa,.—Absol.: evolandi potestas,: longius,: aut saepe ex humili sede sublima evolat, Att. ap. (R): evolare ubi nec Pelopidarum facta neque famam audiam, Poet. ap. ; ; cf. ; ; and R: evolaverunt nebulae sicut aves,: longius (of geese),.—
Transf., to come forth quickly, to rush or spring forth: ex corporum vinculis, tamquam e carcere,; cf. : (hostes) subito ex omnibus partibus silvae evolaverunt,; fin.; cf.: exanimatus evolat e senatu,: rus ex urbe, tamquam e vinculis,: e conspectu,: per medias vias,: ut, lapidem ferro cum caedimus, evolat ignis,.—
Trop.: (almost exclusively in Cic.): ii, quorum animi, spretis corporibus, evolant atque excurrunt foras,: quaestiones omnium perrumpat, evolet ex vestra severitate,; cf. : ex poena,

: quem illi esse in principibus facile sunt passi, evolare altius certe noluerunt,to ascend,: illos dolent evolasse,: sic evolavit oratio, ut, etc.,rose,: tantos processus (Piso) efficiebat, ut evolare, non excurrere videretur,.

la:verb:evolvo.gloss: to roll forth or out; unroll, unfold
senses: to roll forth or out; unroll, unfold
to roll away, pass, elapse, unwind
la:verb:evolvo.html:
ē-volvo, volvi, vŏlūtum, 3 (
per diaeresin ēvŏlŭam, : ēvŏlŭisse,), v. a., to roll out, roll forth; to unroll, unfold (class.).
Lit.: (vis venti) Arbusta evolvens radicibus haurit ab imis,; cf. silvas,: cadavera turribus,: montes corpore,: saxa nudis lacertis,: intestina, et saep.: vestes,to open, unfold,: volumen epistolarum,to open,: panicum furfure,i. e. to cleanse, purge,: quae postquam evolvit,unfolds, evolves, et saep.: amnis prorutam in mare evolvendo terram praealtas voragines facit,; cf. aquas (Araxes),.—
Evolvere se, or mid. evolvi, to roll out, roll forth, glide away: evolvere posset in mare se Xanthus,discharge itself,; cf.: Danubius in Pontum vastis sex fluminibus evolvitur,empties,: species (anguis) evoluta repente,: per humum evolvuntur,roll themselves along,.—
Transf.
To unroll and read a book: evolve diligenter ejus eum librum qui est de animo,: volumina,: fastos,; : versus,: jocos,; cf. transf.: poëtas,; cf. auctores,: auctores penitus,: antiquitatem,—
To draw out a thread, i. e. to spin, said of the Fates: quae seriem fatorum pollice ducunt Longaque ferratis evolvunt saecula pensis,; and pregn., to spin out, i. e. to spin to an end, said of the Fates: tunc, quae dispensant mortalia fata, sorores Debuerant fusos evoluisse meos,.—
To obtain, raise: in hoc triduo Aut terra aut mari alicunde aliqua evolvam argentum tibi,.—
Trop.
In gen.: si qui voluerit animi sui complicatam notionem evolvere, to unroll, i. e. to clear up (the figure being taken from a book), ; cf.: exitum criminis,: promissa evolvit somni,i. e. turns over, revolves,; cf.: secum femineos dolos,: evolutus integumentis dissimulationis (with nudatus),unwrapped, stripped,: evolutus bonis,robbed,; cf.: sede patria rebusque summis,: ex praeda clandestina,driven away,: nullo possum remedio me evolvere ex his turbis,: se omni turba,.—
In partic., to unfold, disclose, narrate: naturam rerum omnium,: oras belli, Enn. ap. (Ann. v. 178 ed. Vahl.): totam deliberationem accuratius,: rem propositam,: condita pectoris,: seriem fati,: haec, et saep.; cf. with a rel.-clause, .—
To roll away, of time, i. e. to pass, elapse: evolutis multis diebus,: cum evolutus esset annus,: evoluto tempore,.

la:verb:evenio.html:
ē-vĕnĭo, vēni, ventum, 4 (
praes. subj. evenat, Enn. ap. ; ; : evenant,), v. n., to come out, come forth.
Lit. (very rare): merses profundo: pulchrior evenit,: tota arundo serius praedicto tempore evenit,comes up, grows up,: sine modo rus eveniat,: Capuam,; cf.: evenit sermo Samuelis Israeli,.—Far more freq. and class.,
Trop.
In gen., to fall out, come to pass, happen; and with alicui, to befall, happen to, betide one (v. 2. accido, II., and 1. contingo, II. B. 3. b.): in hominum aetate multa eveniunt hujusmodi,; cf.: maxime id in rebus publicis evenit,: timebam, ne evenirent ea, quae acciderunt,; cf. ; : quid homini potest turpius, quid viro miserius aut acerbius usu venire? quod tantum evenire dedecus?: quem (sc. tyrannum) si optimates oppresserunt, quod ferme evenit, habet, etc.,; cf.: quod evenit saepius,: quod plerumque evenit,; fin.: hoc in hac conformatione rei publicae non sine magnis principum vitiis evenit,fin.: ut alia Tusculi, alia Romae eveniat saepe tempestas,: quota enim quaeque res evenit praedicta ab istis? aut si evenit quippiam: quid afferri potest, cur non casu id evenerit?: ubi pax evenerat,had been concluded, et saep.: vereor, ne idem eveniat in meas litteras,that the same thing will happen to my letter,.—Impers., it happens (cf.: accidit, incidit, contigit, obtingit, fit), with ut: evenit, senibus ambobus simul Iter ut esset,; so ; Brutus ap. ; ; et saep.; with quod, Enn. ap. (cf. 2. accido): ob id, quod furtum fecit servus, evenit, quo minus eum habere domino liceat,.—With dat.: illi divitiae evenerunt maxumae,; cf.: damna evenerunt maxuma misero mihi,: merito sibi ea evenerunt a me,: cum mihi nihil improviso evenisset,: quibus (improbis) utinam ipsis evenissent ea, quae tum homines precabantur!; cf. et saep.: L. Genucio consuli ea provincia sorte evenit,fell to,; in the same sense without sorte,; ; et saep.: si quid sibi eveniret, if any thing should happen to himself, euphemist. for if he should die, Ruhnk.; ; cf.: si in Pompeio quid humani evenisset, ed. Gerl. (v. 2. accido, II.).—
In partic., to proceed, follow, result (as a consequence) from any thing; to turn out, issue, end in any way (cf. evado, I. B. 2.; evado is used both of

persons and things, but evenio only of things): eventus est alicujus exitus negotii, in quo quaeri solet, quid ex quaque re evenerit, eveniat, eventurum sit, etc.,: ut nobis haec habitatio bona, fausta, felix fortunataque eveniat,: quae (auspicia) sibi secunda evenerint, (al. secunde); cf. : cuncta prospera eventura,; cf. ; : quoniam quae occulte tentaverat, aspera foedaque evenerant (opp. prospere cessere), Kritz.; cf.: si adversa pugna evenisset,: ut ea res mihi magistratuique bene atque feliciter eveniret,; so, bene ac feliciter,; cf. feliciter, * : prospere, (with cadere); so, prospere,; ; : bene,; cf.: male istis eveniat,: vides omnia fere contra ac dicta sint evenisse,; cf.: quod si fors aliter quam voles evenerit,: si quid praeter spem evenit,; ; ; : quoniam haec evenerunt nostra ex sententia,; cf. ; : istaec blanda dicta quo eveniant,; so, quo,; ; cf. quorsum,.—Hence, ēventum, i, n. (acc. to evenio, II.).

An occurrence, chance, event.
In gen. (rare): semper me causae eventorum magis movent quam ipsa eventa,: plurimorum seculorum et eventorum memoria,: si cujusque facti et eventi causa ponetur,.—
In Lucr. opp. conjunctum, of the external conditions, or accidents, of persons and things (as poverty, riches, freedom, etc.), ; ; ; 470 al.—
Alicujus, that which befalls one, experience, fortune: ei qui sciunt quid aliis acciderit, facile ex aliorum eventis suis rationibus possunt providere,: ut te ex nostris eventis communibus admonendum putarem,: fabula rerum eventorumque nostrorum,: cui omnia pendere ex alterius eventis coguntur,: plures aliorum eventis docentur,.—
The issue, consequence, result, effect of an action (cf.: exitus, eventus, successus, obitus, occasus), freq. in Cic., usually plur.: consilia eventis ponderare,; so opp. facta,; Fragm. ap. ; opp. causae,; : quorum praedicta quotidie videat re et eventis refelli,—In sing., .

senses: to become, result, appear, succeed, end up, turn out (as), result in
to arrive at, result in, turn out, come to pass
to end up, have as a result, result in
la:verb:evado.html:
ē-vādo, si, sum, 3 (
perf. sync. evasti, ; ; perf. evadi. Treb. Poll. Trig. Tyr. 5, 6), v. n. and a.
Neutr., to go or come out, go forth (freq. and class.).
Lit.
In gen.: si (apes) ex alvo minus frequentes evadunt,: ex aqua,: ex balineis,: oppido,: undis,: puteo,: abiit, excessit, evasit, erupit,: per praeruptum saxum in Capitolium,: in terram,to disembark, to land,—
In an upward direction: ex abditis sedibus evadere atque exire,: evado ad summi fastigia culminis,mount up, ascend,: ad parietem,: in murum, muros, moenia,; ; : in jugum,: in cacumen,: super capita hostium, et saep.—
In partic., to get away, escape: aut e morbo evasurum aegrotum, aut e periculo navem, aut ex insidiis exercitum,: ex fuga, * : e manibus hostium,: ex judicio,: e tanto periculo,: periculo,: adverso colle, sicuti praeceptum fuerat, evadunt,; cf. fin.; ; et saep.—
Trop.
In gen., to go or come out, pass out, escape: accedit, ut eo facilius animus evadat ex hoc aëre eumque perrumpat, quod, etc.,; cf.: ex corpore (animus),; and: cum ab iis ... evaseris, id Tusc. 1, 41, 98: ad conjecturam,to arrive at,: ne in infinitum quaestio evadat,. —
In an upward direction: nitamur semper ad optima: quod facientes aut evademus in summum, aut certe multos infra nos videbimus,.—
In partic., to turn out, fall out, end in some manner, to have an issue of some kind, to result, to turn to or become something: ex communibus proprii, ex fucosis firmi suffragatores evadunt,; cf. ; : quos judicabat non posse oratores evadere,: fuit autem Athenis adulescens, perfectus Epicureus evaserat,; ; : ita molles mentes evadunt civium,; cf.: juvenis evasit vere indolis regiae,: quod tu ejusmodi evasisti,: nimis saepe secus videmus evadere,.—Of abstract subjects: ut ita fastidiosae mollesque mentes evadant civium, ut, etc.,: si quando aliquod somnium verum evaserit,: vereor ne haec quoque laetitia vana evadat,: quoniam primum vanum inceptum evasisset, et saep.: intellego hercle: sed quo evadas nescio,what you are driving at,: quam timeo, quorsum evadas, where you are coming out in your story, ; : nimia illaec licentia Profecto evadet in aliquod magnum malum,: demiror quid sit, et quo evadat, sum in metu,; cf. : videamus, hoc quorsum evadat,; : huccine (beneficia),to end in this,: in morbos longos,.—
Pregn., to come to pass, be fulfilled: aliquando id, quod somniarimus, evadere,; for which: si somnium verum evasit aliquod,.
Act. (mostly poet. and post-Aug.; not in Cic.), to pass over or pass a thing, to get over, pass beyond, leave behind.
Lit.
In gen.: omnem videbar evasisse viam,: tot urbes,: vada, arva,: amnem,: limen harae,: vestibulum (apes), et saep.—
In an upward direction: sic fata gradus evaserat altos,had mounted the steps,: ardua,to climb, ascend,. —
In partic., to get away, flee, escape from, = effugere: alicujus manus,: loca mortis,: flammam,: angustias,; : nocturnas insidias,: aliquem, Tiber. ap. .—
Trop.
In gen.: vitam, to depart from, i. e. to die, .—
In an upward direction: si haec quoque jam lenius supina perseverantibus studiis evaseris,hast climbed, ascended,.—
In partic., to escape, get rid of: aegritudinem, Lucil. ap. : necem,: gravem casum,: sermones malignorum, et saep.

la:verb:eversus.html:
ēversus, a, um.
Swept out, v. everro.—
Overthrown, v. everto.

la:verb:everto.gloss: to turn upside down, overturn, reverse
senses: to turn upside down, overturn, reverse
to throw down, cause to fall
la:verb:everto.html:
ē-verto or -vorto, ti, sum, 3, v. a.,
to overturn, turn upside down (syn. demolior, destruo, extinguo, diruo, deleo, etc.).
Lit.
In gen. (very rare): aequora ventis,to upturn, agitate,; cf. aquas,: mare,: campum,i. e. to plough,: cervices,to twist, Ruhnk.—More freq. and class. (not in Caes.),
In partic.
To overturn any thing from its position, to overthrow, upset, throw down: naviculam,; ; ; cf. : pinum,; § 130; cf. poët.: Ismara,i. e. the trees of Ismarus,: currum,; cf. equum,—Transf., of persons: eversus,thrown down,; .—Designating the term. ad quem: si quis Athon Pindumve revulsos Sede sua, totos in apertum everteret aequor,; cf.: tecta in dominum,.—
Transf., to overthrow, subvert, destroy: urbes (with diripere),: Carthaginem,: Trojam,: castellum,: funditus arces,.—
To turn out, drive out, expel a man from his possession: ut agro evortat Lesbonicum, quando evortit aedibus,; so, adolescentem bonis,: pupillum fortunis patriis,: eos fortunis omnibus,; : hunc funditus bonis,—
Trop. (Acc. to I. B.)
To overturn, overthrow: ab imo summa,: aliquem non judicio neque disceptatione, sed vi atque impressione evertere,to ruin,: aliquem fortunis omnibus,.—
To overthrow completely, to subvert, ruin, destroy: funditus aratores,: funditus civitates,: eversa per te et perdita civitas,; ; cf. ; : funditus amicitiam,; cf.: penitus virtutem,: totum genus hoc regiae civitatis,: leges, testamenta,; cf. : constitutam philosophiam,; cf. definitionem,: finitionem,: opus,: majestatem dictatoriam et disciplinam militarem,: patrimonium,to waste, squander,: pietatem,: spem,: Crassos, Pompeios,to ruin,: titulum, to erase, Capit. Gord. .

la:verb:evello.gloss: to tear, pull or pluck out
senses: to tear, pull or pluck out
la:verb:evello.html:
ē-vello, velli (; ), post-class., vulsi (; ), vulsum, 3, v. a.,
to tear, pull, or pluck out (class.).
Lit.: linguam se evellisse M. Catoni,: ferrum, * : arborem,: dentes, et saep.: spinas agro,; cf.: ebulum, cicutam e segete, § 55: clavos sepulcris,: statuam de monumento,.— Poet.: odorem e turis glebis (with divellere),: castra obsessa (sc. ex obsidione),i. e. to relieve,.—
To drag away, tear away: ab altari eum,; cf.: lucos tuos de medio tui, id. Micah, 5, 13.—
Trop., to tear out, root out, eradicate, erase (a favorite word of Cicero): radicitus mala,: consules non modo ex memoria sed etiam ex fastis evellendi,: scrupulum ex animo,; cf.: aculeum severitatis,: omnem eorum importunitatem ex intimis mentibus,; cf. : iras (e pectore),.

la:noun:eventus.html:
ēventus, ūs, m.
evenio, II.
.
An occurrence, accident, event; fortune, fate, lot (rare but class.): mihi a peritis in Asia praedictum est, fore eos eventus rerum qui acciderunt,: in incerto reliqui temporis eventu,; ; : maerere hoc ejus (sc. Scipionis) eventu, vereor ne invidi magis quam amici sit,: militum,; cf. ; : navium suarum,: patriae, et saep.: quid reliquis acciderit, qui quosque eventus exciperent,; cf. fin.—Far more freq.,
The (lucky or unlucky) issue, consequence, result of an action (for syn. cf.: eventum, exitus, successus), in sing. and plur.: eventus est alicujus exitus negotii,: in rebus magnis memoriaque dignis consilia primum, deinde acta, postea eventus exspectantur,: etiam amplissimorum virorum consilia ex eventu, non ex voluntate a plerisque probari solent, Balbus et Oppius ap. A: sceleris est poena tristis, et praeter eos eventus, qui sequuntur, per se ipsa maxima est, et saep.: semper ad eventum festinat (poëta), to the end, issue, event, : interim rei eventum experiri,; so with gen.: belli,; ; : pugnae,: ejus diei,: orationis,: dicendi, et saep.— Prov.: eventus docet ... stultorum iste magister est,.—
Esp., good fortune, success: egi ego pro Vareno non sine eventu,: atque illi modo cauti prompti post eventum ac magniloqui erant,: cf.: satis jam eventuum, satis casuum,.—
Personified: Bonus Eventus,Good Success, a guardian deity of the Roman husbandmen,; ; ; in the dat. also: BONO EVENTO,; cf.: DEO SANCTO EVENTO,.

la:noun:evocator.gloss: One who calls troops to arms, recruiter, summoner
senses: One who calls troops to arms, recruiter, summoner
la:noun:evocator.html:
ēvŏcātor, ōris, m.
id.
,
one who calls to arms: servorum et civium perditorum,.

la:verb:evinco.html:
ē-vinco, vici, victum, 3, v. a. (not anteAug.).
To overcome completely, to conquer, vanquish: evicit omnia assuetus praedae miles,: imbelles, Aeduos,.—
Transf. beyond the milit. sphere (freq.): lacrimis evicta,overcome,: dolore,to induce,: precibus,; : blandimentis vitae,: donis,i. e. to bribe, et saep.: in gaudium evicta domus,moved,; cf.: ad miserationem,: oppositas moles gurgite (amnis),.—Of dangerous places, to pass by in safely: Charybdin remis (rates),: fretum,: aequora,: litora (Ponti),: os Ponti,: nubes (solis imago),: somnos,: morbos,: dolorem (with perferre),: superbiam (miseratio),: luridaque evictos effugit umbra rogos, vanquished, i. e. from which it has struggled free, . platanus caelebs Evincet ulmos,i. e. will supplant them,; cf.: evincit herbas lupinum,.—Less freq.,
To carry one's point, to prevail, succeed in a thing.
In gen., with ut: evincunt instando, ut, etc.,; ; so,; ; .—With rel.-clause, .—
In partic., jurid. t. t., to recover one's property by judicial decision: sive tota res evincatur sive pars, etc.,; sq.; cf. , and v. evictio.—*
Transf., for convinco (2. β), to succeed in proving, to demonstrate, evince: si puerilius his ratio esse evincet amare,will evince,.

la:verb:evoco.gloss: to summon, to call out, to call forth
senses: to summon, to call out, to call forth
la:verb:evoco.html:
ē-vŏco, āvi, ātum, 1, v. a.,
to call out, call forth; to bring out, draw forth (class. —syn. invito, cito, etc.).
Lit.
In gen.: (Tullia) evocavit virum e curia,: gubernatorem a navi huc,: aliquem huc foras,; ; : hinc foras,: intus foras,; : aliquem ante ostium,: mercatores undique ad se,to call together, summon,; cf.: aliquem litteris,: nostros ad pugnam,to call out, challenge,.—
Transf., of inanimate things (mostly post-Aug.): sucum quasi per siphonem,; cf.: materiam ad extremas partes fricatione,: abortum,: ut in longitudinem potius quam in latitudinem evocetur (salix),; cf.: vitis evocata ad fructum,.—
In partic.
Relig. t. t.: deum, to call a deity out of a besieged city, ; ; cf. ; —
In civil and milit. lang., to call out, summon to appear, sc. soldiers to military service: (Metellus) evocat ad se Centuripinorum magistratus et decemprimos,; cf. : senatum omnem ad se Decetiam,: principes cujusque civitatis ad se,; cf. : omnes (senatores),: centuriones, et saep.: nominatim nobilissimum et fortissimum quemque ex omnibus civitatibus,; cf. ; ; : reliquas legiones ex hibernis,: equites ex municipiis,: hanc (legionem) initio tumultus,fin.: magnam partem oppidanorum ad bellum,; cf. fin.: multos undique spe praemiorum,; cf. ; —
Trop.: probitas non praemiorum mercedibus evocata,called forth, elicited,; cf. : misericordia nullius oratione evocata,called forth, produced,; cf. indicium,: iram, Sen. de Ira, 3, 8: risum lugentibus,: ad aliquem honorem evocatus,: eas (tacitas cogitationes) evocat in medium,: aliquem in saevitiam ac violentiam, Sen. de Ira, 3, 5; cf.: aliquem in laetitiam, al.; cf. Gron. .—Hence, Part.: ēvŏcā-tus, a, um; as subst. (cf. evoco, B. 2.): ēvŏcāti, ōrum, m., soldiers who, having served out their time, were called upon to do military duty as volunteers, veterans, ; ; ;

la:verb:evincio.html:
ē-vincĭo, nxi, nctum, 4, v. a.,
to bind up, to bind or wind round with something (not ante-Aug., and mostly poet.): simul diademate caput Tiridatis evinxit,; cf. .—More freq. in the part. perf.: viridi Mnestheus evinctus oliva,; cf. palmae,i. e. wound round with the cestus,: comae (sc. vittā),: evincta pudicā Fronde manus,crowned with laurel,.—With acc. respectiv.: puniceo stabis suras evincta cothurno,; ; ; ; .—
To bind: evincta lacerandum traditi dextra, (dub.; al. victa).

la:verb:eveho.html:
ē-vĕho, xi, ctum, 3, v. a.,
to carry out or forth, to convey out, lead forth (rare but class.).
Lit.: omnia (signa) ex fanis, ex locis publicis palam plaustris evecta exportataque esse,: aquas ex planis locis,; cf. : stercus (with exportare),: merces (opp. inveho),; et saep.: incaute se evehentes Masinissa excipiebat,throwing themselves out, rushing out,: naves in altum,.—In an upward direction; palmaque nobilis Terrarum dominos evehit ad deos, raises aloft, elevates, * ; cf.: aliquem ad aethera,: ad auras,: in caelum,.—
Reflex., to ride out or forth, to move out, move forth, proceed, advance, go, spread: evectus effreno equo,springing forwards,: cf. longius,: de nocte,: evecti Aegeo mari Delum trajecerunt,; cf. : ad portum,: in altum,: ratibus ad regem, et saep.: in ancoras evehi,to run foul of the anchors,.— With the acc. of the place: evectus os amnis,—
To carry up, to convey upwards: ut in collem Esquiliarium eveheretur,.—
Trop.
To carry forth, take out, spread abroad: ut semel e Piraeeo eloquentia evecta est, omnes peragravit insulas,went forth,; cf.: fama ejus evecta insulas,: spe vana evectus,carried forwards,; cf. inconsultius,; and, longius,: magicae vanitates in tantum evectae, ut, etc.,: evectus sum longius,I have made too long a digression,.—
In an upward direction, to raise or lift up, to elevate: quem usque in tertium consulatum amicitia Principis evexerat,; cf.: aliquos ad consulatus,; and: imperium ad summum fastigium,; cf.: ad magnum culmen,.—In the part. perf., advanced, promoted: consiliarii in summum evecti fastigium,; cf. : privatum supra modum evectae opes,increased,.— With dat.: aliquem evehere summis honoribus,.

la:verb:evalesco.gloss: to get stronger, to grow, to be strengthened
senses: to get stronger, to grow, to be strengthened
la:verb:evalesco.html:
ē-vălesco, lŭi, 3,
v. inch. n., to become strong, increase in strength, to increase, grow (cf.: vix illa, quae παραγόμενα vocant, nobis permittimus, sed hoc feliciter, evaluit, ; not ante-Aug.).

la:verb:evenio#2.html:
ē-vĕnĭo, vēni, ventum, 4 (
praes. subj. evenat, Enn. ap. ; ; : evenant,), v. n., to come out, come forth.
Lit. (very rare): merses profundo: pulchrior evenit,: tota arundo serius praedicto tempore evenit,comes up, grows up,: sine modo rus eveniat,: Capuam,; cf.: evenit sermo Samuelis Israeli,.—Far more freq. and class.,
Trop.
In gen., to fall out, come to pass, happen; and with alicui, to befall, happen to, betide one (v. 2. accido, II., and 1. contingo, II. B. 3. b.): in hominum aetate multa eveniunt hujusmodi,; cf.: maxime id in rebus publicis evenit,: timebam, ne evenirent ea, quae acciderunt,; cf. ; : quid homini potest turpius, quid viro miserius aut acerbius usu venire? quod tantum evenire dedecus?: quem (sc. tyrannum) si optimates oppresserunt, quod ferme evenit, habet, etc.,; cf.: quod evenit saepius,: quod plerumque evenit,; fin.: hoc in hac conformatione rei publicae non sine magnis principum vitiis evenit,fin.: ut alia Tusculi, alia Romae eveniat saepe tempestas,: quota enim quaeque res evenit praedicta ab istis? aut si evenit quippiam: quid afferri potest, cur non casu id evenerit?: ubi pax evenerat,had been concluded, et saep.: vereor, ne idem eveniat in meas litteras,that the same thing will happen to my letter,.—Impers., it happens (cf.: accidit, incidit, contigit, obtingit, fit), with ut: evenit, senibus ambobus simul Iter ut esset,; so ; Brutus ap. ; ; et saep.; with quod, Enn. ap. (cf. 2. accido): ob id, quod furtum fecit servus, evenit, quo minus eum habere domino liceat,.—With dat.: illi divitiae evenerunt maxumae,; cf.: damna evenerunt maxuma misero mihi,: merito sibi ea evenerunt a me,: cum mihi nihil improviso evenisset,: quibus (improbis) utinam ipsis evenissent ea, quae tum homines precabantur!; cf. et saep.: L. Genucio consuli ea provincia sorte evenit,fell to,; in the same sense without sorte,; ; et saep.: si quid sibi eveniret, if any thing should happen to himself, euphemist. for if he should die, Ruhnk.; ; cf.: si in Pompeio quid humani evenisset, ed. Gerl. (v. 2. accido, II.).—
In partic., to proceed, follow, result (as a consequence) from any thing; to turn out, issue, end in any way (cf. evado, I. B. 2.; evado is used both of

persons and things, but evenio only of things): eventus est alicujus exitus negotii, in quo quaeri solet, quid ex quaque re evenerit, eveniat, eventurum sit, etc.,: ut nobis haec habitatio bona, fausta, felix fortunataque eveniat,: quae (auspicia) sibi secunda evenerint, (al. secunde); cf. : cuncta prospera eventura,; cf. ; : quoniam quae occulte tentaverat, aspera foedaque evenerant (opp. prospere cessere), Kritz.; cf.: si adversa pugna evenisset,: ut ea res mihi magistratuique bene atque feliciter eveniret,; so, bene ac feliciter,; cf. feliciter, * : prospere, (with cadere); so, prospere,; ; : bene,; cf.: male istis eveniat,: vides omnia fere contra ac dicta sint evenisse,; cf.: quod si fors aliter quam voles evenerit,: si quid praeter spem evenit,; ; ; : quoniam haec evenerunt nostra ex sententia,; cf. ; : istaec blanda dicta quo eveniant,; so, quo,; ; cf. quorsum,.—Hence, ēventum, i, n. (acc. to evenio, II.).

An occurrence, chance, event.
In gen. (rare): semper me causae eventorum magis movent quam ipsa eventa,: plurimorum seculorum et eventorum memoria,: si cujusque facti et eventi causa ponetur,.—
In Lucr. opp. conjunctum, of the external conditions, or accidents, of persons and things (as poverty, riches, freedom, etc.), ; ; ; 470 al.—
Alicujus, that which befalls one, experience, fortune: ei qui sciunt quid aliis acciderit, facile ex aliorum eventis suis rationibus possunt providere,: ut te ex nostris eventis communibus admonendum putarem,: fabula rerum eventorumque nostrorum,: cui omnia pendere ex alterius eventis coguntur,: plures aliorum eventis docentur,.—
The issue, consequence, result, effect of an action (cf.: exitus, eventus, successus, obitus, occasus), freq. in Cic., usually plur.: consilia eventis ponderare,; so opp. facta,; Fragm. ap. ; opp. causae,; : quorum praedicta quotidie videat re et eventis refelli,—In sing., .
